newsitem.title: USA: Four-nation peace talks on Korea expected in August.
newsitem.headline: Four-nation peace talks on Korea expected in August.

text.p: Four-nation peace talks between North and South Korea, the United States and China are expected to be held on Aug. 5 in Geneva, sources close to preparatory talks said on Monday.

The proposed four-party negotiations would aim to replace the armistice with a formal peace treaty. The armistice ended the fighting in the 1950-53 Korean War, but technically not the war on the Korean peninsula.
The sources said the date would be announced officially later on Monday at the end of a new round of talks among U.S. officials and the two Koreas.

North Korean and South Korean delegation leaders earlier told each other they hoped for good results from their Monday meeting, a follow-up to talks in March and April to discuss a proposal by Washington and Seoul for the four-nation peace talks that would include China.

According to a U.S. official, the North Korean delegation leader, Vice Foreign Minister Kim Gye Gwan, said: "Last time we were concerned that there might be a premature baby, but this time we're not concerned about a premature baby."
The South Korean delegation is led by Deputy Foreign Minister Song Yong Shik and the U.S. delegation by Charles Kartman, the acting assistant secretary of state for East Asian and Pacific Affairs
Communist North Korea, threatened by famine, agreed in principle in April to join the peace talks but linked its participation to food aid and an end to U.S. trade sanctions.
Political analysts say Pyongyang has agreed to join the four-way talks in a policy shift designed to hold the reclusive state together.
They say that with famine and a ruined economy, the Stalinist government needs to repair its relationship with Western countries who could provide much-needed assistance.
Nevertheless, the Monday talks opened with North Korea wanting more commitments for food aid, according to a South Korean official.

"Basically North Korea is taking the same position as they took in the April meeting, but we are trying to make them come around to our position," delegate Yu Myung Hwan of the South Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs told reporters.

"North Korea wanted us to commit a specific amount of food aid before they would come to the preparatory talks ... and we were trying to delink the food and the four-party talks," he said during a lunch break.
In the relaxed exchanges before Monday's meeting began, Kartman joked with his counterparts.

A U.S. official quoted Kartman as saying, "Let me tell you about American boxing ...", a reference to Saturday's World Boxing Association heavyweight title fight in which challenger Mike Tyson was disqualified for biting both ears of champion Evander Holyfield.
